title: A midnight reporting discrepancy
summary: Explore an unfamiliar ingestion pipeline and fix daily totals with time zones, refunds, and repeated deliveries.

stages.title: Understand the contract
stages.brief: Explore an unfamiliar ingestion pipeline and fix daily totals with time zones, refunds, and repeated deliveries. Preserve the documented public interface. Use only Python 3.11 standard-library modules.
requirements: Preserve build_report(lines), read_events(lines), and aggregate(events). build_report accepts a one-pass iterable of JSON strings; blank lines are ignored.

Each nonblank line is an object with nonempty string event_id/customer_id, kind purchase or refund, positive integer amount_cents (not bool), and an ISO 8601 occurred_at with an explicit timezone. Extra fields may be ignored.
Normalize occurred_at to UTC before assigning its calendar day. Purchases add cents; refunds subtract cents. Refund-only and net-zero rows are retained.
event_id is globally unique within one report. An identical semantic retry counts once; a conflicting retry raises ValueError. Equivalent timestamps with different offsets represent the same instant.
Return dictionaries with customer_id, day (YYYY-MM-DD in UTC), and net_cents, sorted by customer_id then day. Do not mutate caller inputs.
Malformed records raise ValueError whose message includes the original physical line number. Conflicting IDs raise ValueError without a required line number. No partial report is returned on failure.

stages.title: Implement the change
stages.brief: Make the smallest coherent change that satisfies the disclosed contract.
requirements: Preserve public interfaces and existing valid behavior.

stages.title: Verify the behavior
stages.brief: Run checks and inspect failures before finishing.
requirements: Run public checks and add a targeted boundary or regression check.
Identify behavior that your tests do not establish.

stages.title: Defend your decisions
stages.brief: Explain the submitted code and its remaining limits.
requirements: Use concrete code or test evidence.
Describe one alternative and its trade-off.

rubric.name: Repository comprehension
rubric.description: Trace ingestion, normalization, aggregation, and output contracts.

anchors.strong: Explains module responsibilities and puts validation/time normalization and aggregation logic in appropriate boundaries.
anchors.developing: Fixes one output symptom but misses an ingestion or aggregation boundary.
anchors.needsWork: Changes output without understanding where timestamps and amounts enter the pipeline.

rubric.name: Event semantics
rubric.description: Honor UTC days, refund signs, deduplication, and conflict behavior.

anchors.strong: Normalizes timezone-aware events, compares semantic retry payloads, and preserves signed and zero totals.
anchors.developing: Gets basic totals right but misses a retry, timezone, or zero-total case.
anchors.needsWork: Counts retries/refunds incorrectly or groups by the sender-local calendar date.

rubric.name: Diagnostic evidence
rubric.description: Verify failure messages and representative event sequences.

anchors.strong: Tests cross-midnight offsets, duplicate/conflicting events, invalid lines, and sorted outputs.
anchors.developing: Covers normal purchases but little failure or boundary behavior.
anchors.needsWork: Only checks a simple positive total and assumes the pipeline is correct.

probes.question: Which module owns input normalization, and how does that decision affect the aggregation code?
When are two differently written timestamps the same retry, and when is a duplicate a conflict?
Which event sequence did you use to distinguish local midnight from the UTC reporting day?

hints: Trace build_report through parser.py and aggregation.py. Locate where an event becomes a calendar day and where its sign is chosen.
Parse and validate input once, normalize timestamps to UTC, and deduplicate using event identity plus the semantic payload.
Use datetime.astimezone(timezone.utc) before taking date(). Track seen event IDs and compare customer, kind, amount, and normalized instant. Add physical line numbers during parsing.

drills.title: Trace an event across boundaries
drills.exercise: Construct two offset timestamps for one instant near midnight. Show their UTC bucket, then add a refund and a duplicate and calculate the expected net total.

drills.title: Compare semantic retries
drills.exercise: Construct two JSON records with differently written offsets for the same instant. Count them once; then change the amount or customer under the same ID and verify rejection.

drills.title: Preserve diagnostic context
drills.exercise: Place a blank line before a valid event and then malformed JSON. Assert the physical error line. Add a refund-only day, a zero-net day, and out-of-order customers to verify the output contract.
